ImageDescription.value:
Seen here is a Fiery Skipper Butterfly feeding with the "red guy," also called a Snowberry Clearwing (hummingbird) Moth. Marty calls these guys "flying shrimp." flickr.com/photos/martytdx/197907873/ Both enjoyed the bounty of the thistle patch which has now gone to seed and crumbled away.

The hummingbird moths are mistaken for hummingbirds because they can hover just like hummingbirds. These moths are bumble bee mimics due to their black and yellow colors and can give quite a scare if they fly up on you suddenly. flickr.com/photos/drphotomoto/2643807951/

ImageDescription.value: European honeysuckle is a species of flowering plant in the family Caprifoliaceae native to much of Europe, North Africa, Turkey and the Caucasus. It is found as far north as southern Norway and Sweden. In the evening, they emit a strong, pleasant scent, while the flowering rests during the bright and warm part of the day. Night-flying moths such as the hummingbird hawk-moth can detect the scent of honeysuckle flowers up to a quarter of a mile away.

ImageDescription.value:
The snowberry clearwing moth (Hemaris diffinis) is known by several names including "hummingbird moth", "flying lobster", and "lobster tail". The caterpillars of this species need snowberry, honeysuckle, or dogbanes as host plants. Adults feed on nectar from thistles, snowberries, hawkweeds, lilacs, and violets, among other flowers. This moth was found while building fence on the Mayer Waterfowl Production Area in Logan County, North Dakota.
Photo Credit: Krista Lundgren/USFWS
